To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Rhizobius meliloti nitrogen fixation genes nifA, nifHDK are activated by the K. pneumoniaes nifA gene.

the nifA product from the free-living bacterium Klebsiemia pneumoniae activates the nitrogenase promoter of Rhizobium, the bacterium responsible for fixing nitrogen in root nodules of the legume plant alfalfa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the nif promoters and with the identification of a nifA gene regulatory function in R. meliloti.
the regulation of the Rhizobial nitrogen-fixing system.
the molecular genetics of the nitrogenase gene cluster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nifA gene from Klebsiella has been shown to be able to activate the Rhizobius meliloti nifiHDK operon promoter.
the Klebsiella nifA product is capable of activating transcription from a promoter of the nitrogen-fixing bacterium Rhizobium.

the K. pneumoniaespecific nifA gene, which is required for expression of all nif genes in this bacterium, is able to activate the R. meliloti nift promoter, which is normally expressed only in the differentiated bacteroid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rhizobial nodule bacteroids, like the K. pneumonia bacteroids, have a nitrogenase gene promoter activated by the nifA product.
the K. pneumoniaes nifA gene is a positive regulatory gene for the expression of nif genes in Rhizobium.
the nifA gene of K. pneumoniae is able to activate the expression of the nifH gene in R. meliloti.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of the nitrogenase genes in K. pneumoniae, a free-living, facultative anaerobe, and in the symbiotic rhizobia is more similar than was expected.
a single transcriptional regulatory protein from a free-living bacterium is able to activate the nif promoter from a symbiotic nitrogen-fixing bacterium.
the nifA gene is a key regulatory gene that is involved in the expression of nitrogenase in both rhizobia and enteric bacteria.
